claims.statement: Syntactic ambiguity can increase processing and revision demands, thereby increasing cognitive load during sentence comprehension.
Longer syntactic dependencies increase memory and integration demands during language processing, linking dependency length to cognitive load.
Higher contextual predictability generally facilitates language processing, while unexpected continuations increase processing difficulty; the relation is probabilistic and context-sensitive.
Personal importance and relevance of an issue increase motivation to process persuasive information, linking motivational goal importance with persuasion involvement.
Injunctive norm messages can threaten autonomy or self-relevant values and thereby evoke reactance or resistance under some conditions.
Injunctive norm pressure can undermine intrinsic motivation or trust when recipients experience the norm as controlling or misaligned with valued motives.

Claim-support structure provides the message-side organization through which receiver-side argument quality can be assessed, although structural completeness alone does not guarantee a strong argument.
Concessions and two-sided structures can change perceived credibility or trustworthiness, with effects depending on the content conceded and whether counterarguments are refuted.
Clearer specification of the immediate next action can reduce implementation ambiguity and procedural burden, but clarity does not create motivation by itself.
Request wording and framing can alter behavioral compliance, with effects moderated by prior behavior, norms, reciprocity, authority, and recipient interpretation.
More explicit action requests can reduce ambiguity about the requested behavior, but their compliance effect depends on pressure, autonomy, social context, and friction.
Emotional appeals can shift attitudes and persuasive outcomes, but effects differ across emotions, appeals, audiences, and contexts.
Character identification is associated with narrative persuasion and can contribute to changes in evaluations, alongside transportation and other narrative processes.
